correctness.rationale: The defining STFT reduces exactly to two real shifted Hermite Gaussians. Nonshared coefficient zeros restrict frequency solutions to two time slices; shared Hermite roots give exactly the full horizontal-in-time lines. An explicit repeated-Rolle argument bounds each degree-n Gaussian-exponential branch by 2n+1 scalar multiplicities, and parity improves the sum to 4n+1. Uniform asymptotic root separation and the implicit function theorem construct 4n+1 distinct nondegenerate zeros for sufficiently large separation. The 95 reported numerical checks supplement the analytic proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Almost-sure isolation of white-noise zeros is not an all-deterministic-signal result and cannot exclude specifically tuned continuum resonances. Multiwindow ambiguity zeros concern a different bilinear function. A standard Chebyshev zero-bound lemma supplies one ingredient but alone neither gives the sharp two-slice joint bound nor establishes all resonance lines and their occurrence.

value.rationale: This is a uniform sharp, attained complexity ceiling across all Hermite orders for a natural two-frequency calibration signal, together with the exact finite list of exceptional gaps and entire line frequencies where the zero geometry ceases to be discrete. The higher-order full-line resonance mechanism is absent from Gaussian and first-Hermite cases, and informs how zeros of deterministic signals differ from almost-sure white-noise zeros. It is a motivated infinite-family structural classification, not a single arbitrary count.
